title: Burst-safe reserved pools: negotiated burst envelopes, GPU-class arbitration, and predictive autoscale throttles
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Customers repeatedly ask for predictable reserved throughput but also the ability to absorb short-term peaks without overcommitting budget. This proposal outlines a triage and negotiation flow plus implementation guardrails for 'burst envelopes'—contracted burst allowances on top of a reserved baseline—and an adaptive autoscale throttler that uses predictive signals and GPU-class arbitration (dedicated vs preemptible) to meet SLAs while minimizing cost.

Goals: 1) Provide a clear intake template that captures steady-state QPS, P95 latency target, burst frequency/duration, and acceptable fallback GPU class. 2) Define negotiation knobs (baseline reserved throughput, burst envelope size, burst credits refill policy, and overage pricing model). 3) Design an adaptive autoscaling policy that uses short-horizon demand forecasts to prefer reserved-GPU handling for latency-critical requests and spill to preemptible or lower-GPU-class pools for best-effort bursts. 4) Create monitoring and billing signals to surface burst usage and SLA adherence to customers.

Scope decisions: - This ticket covers product spec, intake questionnaire updates, SLA bands for burst-capable contracts, and high-level orchestration policies. Implementation tasks (runtime changes, kernel tuning, billing engine) will be tracked in linked ENG tickets. - We will initially support a single burst-envelope shape (continuous credit bucket with 1h replenishment; configurable) and three GPU-class labels (premium-reserved, standard-reserved, preemptible-fallback).

Accepted customer scenarios: - Low-latency chat + occasional heavy embedding syncs: needs P95 <= 120ms for chat; sustained baseline 200 QPS; up to 2x burst for 10 min/hour. - Large-batch embedding pipelines: baseline 50 QPS, bursts to 500 QPS for up to 30m/day with tolerance for degraded latency on fallback.

Negotiation template (to add to intake flow): - Baseline throughput (tokens/sec or QPS): 
- P95 latency objective and maximum tolerated degraded tier latency: 
- Burst profile: frequency (times/day), typical duration (mins), expected peak multiplier: 
- Preferred fallback GPU classes (ordered): 
- Cost sensitivity: prefer predictable monthly commit vs pay-for-burst margin: 
- Compliance notes (data residency, private pools): 

Autoscale/Orchestration policy (high-level): 1) Run predictive short-horizon (5–15m) demand model in control plane using moving-window feature set (recent QPS, scheduled jobs, customer traffic patterns). 2) If forecast > baseline and within customer's burst envelope, enable burst workers on same GPU class. 3) If forecast > baseline + envelope, evaluate fallback: a) spill to preemptible pool if customer accepted that class (and latency slack allowed), b) apply rate-limited queuing or soft-fail with degraded response if customer disallowed preemptible fallback. 4) Apply per-customer throttles to avoid noisy-neighbor impacts. 5) Record token-level latency and cost attribution for every burst event in console.

Metrics and SLOs: - Burst adherence: percent of burst minutes where baseline+burst handled without fallback (target 95% week-over-week). - SLA violations: count and percentile of P95 breaches during bursts. - Cost delta: measured token cost during burst vs steady-state. - Customer visibility: dashboard widget showing burst budget consumption, refill schedule, and incident log.

Rollout plan: 1) Pilot with two existing enterprise customers who requested burst capabilities and agreed to testing (get legal sign-off on pricing). 2) Implement intake form updates and contract templates (PM + Legal + Sales). 3) Deliver simple autoscale policy knobs and a telemetry dashboard (ENG scope). 4) Run a 4-week pilot, measure metrics, iterate pricing and envelope defaults. 5) General availability after pilot + pricing approval.

Open questions / decisions needed: - Default envelope refill cadence: 1h vs 24h (ops and finance input needed). - Overage pricing model: flat per-token surcharge vs tiered burst credits. - Whether to support cross-customer burst pooling (reserved pool sharing) in initial launch. - Exact telemetry retention window for burst audit logs (30d vs 90d).

Stakeholders: Sales (enterprise AE), Legal, Finance (pricing), Infra SRE, Runtime Engineering, Console UX.

Acceptance criteria: - Intake form available and validated with two pilot customers. - PM-approved negotiation template and pricing proposal. - ENG has scoped autoscale policy and created dependency tickets. - Pilot kickoff scheduled with monitoring dashboards and billing flags in place.
